title: Bind supervisor intake to verified Python dependencies through existing bootstrap and promotion flow
rework_note: Reworked after Codex's 2026-09-05T02:10:47Z reject of head cbea5c308bf2994e7ce1b3c238f39ab1374582b0. That review found four real defects in the first delivery, each addressed below: (1) fresh-host bootstrap imported cryptography with the ambient python3 before the supervisor venv existed; (2) the dependency preflight checked distribution metadata only, never enforced the requirements.txt version specifiers, and never imported the module; (3) sync-dev-root pip-installed into the one fixed venv directory a running incumbent supervisor already launched from, before any preflight ran; (4) no real subprocess test proved signed dev-bridge packet intake actually works under an interpreter built the way these scripts build one.

owned: supervisor Python interpreter selection and dependency preflight (provision_live_supervisor_config.py, promote_supervisor_runtime.py)
scoped .orchestrator/requirements.txt dependency contract for the supervisor runtime only
fresh-host venv provisioning wired into scripts/bootstrap-orchestrator-runtime.sh and scripts/sync-dev-root.sh, now per-candidate-SHA rather than one fixed path
a real subprocess signed dev-bridge packet intake test under a bootstrap-style venv (.orchestrator/development_bridge/tests/test_dev_bridge_inbox_bootstrap_python_runtime.py)
not_changing: scripts/ai_status.py, task archive, and TaskStore (owned by the separate archive-reconciliation prerequisite)
signed packet validation, bridge signing keys, or dev-bridge intake logic itself
supervisor tick-level imports or a second dispatcher/cron/launcher
scripts/supervisor_watchdog_install.py (already restarts from the recorded watchdog.supervisor_command, requires no interpreter-selection change)
composes_with: root-coordinated exact-version governed promotion on the live host after merge

failure_reproduction.case: On 2026-09-05 the live promoted supervisor (PID 96329, source 20282eba2ce2304560ab7eab0cd27af824a22b8b) launched with /usr/bin/python3 -- which has cryptography but not pydantic -- so the main loop stayed healthy while every dev-bridge packet drain failed with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pydantic'.
root_causes: scripts/bootstrap-orchestrator-runtime.sh and scripts/sync-dev-root.sh never passed --python to promote_supervisor_runtime.py, so it defaulted to sys.executable (the ambient interpreter running the bootstrap/sync script itself)

scripts/provision_live_supervisor_config.py resolved --python with Path(...).resolve(), which fully dereferences a venv's bin/python symlink chain back to the base interpreter before CPython's own pyvenv.cfg lookup can run, silently losing every venv-provided package even when a venv path was explicitly passed

(found in review, fixed in rework) scripts/bootstrap-orchestrator-runtime.sh generated the dev-bridge Ed25519 keypair -- which imports cryptography -- using the ambient python3 before the supervisor venv was ever created, so a fresh host with no ambient cryptography could not bootstrap at all

(found in review, fixed in rework) validate_python_dependencies() called importlib.metadata.version() only: it never parsed or enforced the requirements.txt version specifier and never imported the module, so a wrong-version or broken-native-extension install could report a passing preflight

(found in review, fixed in rework) scripts/sync-dev-root.sh pip-installed every promotion into one fixed $PANTHEON_DEPLOY_ROOT/runtime/supervisor-python directory -- the same directory a currently running incumbent supervisor had already launched from -- before any preflight ran, so a partial or failed install could break the live incumbent regardless of whether the candidate was ever accepted
failure_reproduction.reproduction: test_cli_preserves_a_venv_symlink_path_instead_of_resolving_it (scripts/test_provision_live_supervisor_config.py) builds a real filesystem symlink to sys.executable and proves the pre-fix .resolve() call would have collapsed it; test_validate_python_dependencies_rejects_a_de_virtualized_interpreter proves the base /usr/bin/python3 on this host fails the same pydantic-dependency preflight that was silently bypassed live; test_bare_venv_without_the_dependency_contract_fails_closed (new, see below) proves a venv built the same way as bootstrap/sync but never given .orchestrator/requirements.txt fails the real signed-packet drain instead of looking healthy.

implementation.dependency_contract: .orchestrator/requirements.txt pins pydantic>=2.9,<3 and cryptography>=42,<51 -- the supervisor's own bridge/task-store imports, not the product BFF's full dependency set.
implementation.interpreter_selection_fix: provision_live_supervisor_config.py now stores Path(args.python).expanduser().absolute() instead of .resolve(), preserving a venv invocation path so CPython's own symlink-chasing pyvenv.cfg lookup still runs at supervisor launch.
implementation.dependency_preflight: validate_python_dependencies() in provision_live_supervisor_config.py now parses each requirements.txt line into (distribution_name, specifier), then runs a probe entirely inside the exact candidate interpreter that (a) calls importlib.metadata.version() for the real installed version, (b) enforces the declared specifier with a self-contained PEP440-lite numeric comparator (no external 'packaging' dependency needed inside the probe), and (c) calls importlib.import_module() on the package -- so a wrong version or a broken native extension (e.g. an unloadable pydantic_core) fails the preflight instead of passing on metadata alone. A new --validate-python-dependencies-only CLI mode runs just this check (used by sync-dev-root.sh's explicit preflight below) without requiring --repo-config/--live-config/--status-root. The auto_integrator import used by the full config-render lock is now lazy (imported inside main(), not at module import time) so the lightweight preflight-only paths do not need that module's own dependency surface. Wired into provision's CLI (_main_locked) before any config write, and into promote's render_v2_config() -- called before _replace_supervisor_locked's try block, i.e. before seal/stop/write/launch -- so a failed preflight raises before the incumbent supervisor, live config, leases, or watchdog/cron binding are touched.
implementation.fresh_host_provisioning: scripts/bootstrap-orchestrator-runtime.sh materializes the immutable command root first, then creates $PANTHEON_DEPLOY_ROOT/runtime/supervisor-python/<exact-command-SHA> via `python3 -m venv` and installs that exact command root's own .orchestrator/requirements.txt into it, BEFORE generating the dev-bridge Ed25519 keypair -- which now runs under that venv's python3, never the ambient one, so a fresh host with no ambient cryptography can still bootstrap. scripts/sync-dev-root.sh does the same against the exact candidate being promoted, but the venv directory is now versioned per exact candidate SHA ($PANTHEON_SUPERVISOR_PYTHON_DIR-or-default parent + /<target_sha>) instead of one fixed path: an install for a new candidate can never touch the directory backing a different, already-promoted SHA, so the incumbent (and every prior verified environment, usable for rollback) is untouched by construction rather than by hoping the preflight runs before any mutation. sync-dev-root.sh also now runs the new --validate-python-dependencies-only preflight explicitly against the candidate's own provision_live_supervisor_config.py right after the pip install and before invoking promote-supervisor-runtime.sh, logging the untouched incumbent root on failure.
implementation.watchdog_restart_preservation: No change was needed in scripts/supervisor_watchdog_install.py or .orchestrator/supervisor_watchdog.py: both already restart the supervisor by re-executing the recorded watchdog.supervisor_command from the live config, so the accepted --python path survives every subsequent restart once promotion renders it correctly.

passed.command: PYTHONPATH=.orchestrator <clean venv with pydantic 2.13.5 + cryptography 50.0.1 + pytest 9.1.1>/bin/python3 -m pytest -q .orchestrator/development_bridge/tests/test_dev_bridge_inbox_bootstrap_python_runtime.py
passed.result: 2 passed -- genuinely queues and drains a real Ed25519-signed DevTaskPacket through a fresh `python3 -m venv` + `pip install -r .orchestrator/requirements.txt` interpreter (test_bootstrap_style_venv_drains_a_real_signed_packet), and proves a bare venv built the same way but never given the requirements file fails the real drain instead of looking healthy (test_bare_venv_without_the_dependency_contract_fails_closed)

runner.interpreter: checkout-scoped .venv-pantheon provisioned via scripts/dev/provision_python_distribution.py for the shell-wiring suites; the new signed-intake test was additionally verified under a disposable `python3 -m venv` + `pip install pytest pydantic cryptography` interpreter (pydantic 2.13.5, cryptography 50.0.1) because the shared main-worktree .venv this host's provisioning normally inherits from has an unrelated, pre-existing typing_extensions/pydantic_core version mismatch that also fails collection for the pre-existing .orchestrator/development_bridge/tests/test_dev_bridge_inbox_cli.py -- confirmed unrelated to this change since that file is untouched by this task

root_coordination_note: This delivery is source-only, per the SA/SD: exact-version governed promotion after merge, confirming the launched interpreter, automatic pending -> processed admission and canonical readback, a fresh heartbeat, and worker-lease preservation are coordinated by root and are not claimed here.
residual_notes: The new .orchestrator/development_bridge/tests/test_dev_bridge_inbox_bootstrap_python_runtime.py is not yet wired into .github/workflows/branch-ci.yml's tooling smoke gate; it does a real `pip install` and is slower than the existing sys.executable-based CLI tests, so wiring it into CI is left as a follow-up decision for whoever owns that workflow rather than bundled into this source-only fix.

review_decision.note: Independently verify: (1) the bootstrap ordering fix (venv before keypair, keypair generation runs under the venv's python3 not ambient); (2) the dependency preflight now enforces version specifiers and does a real import, not just metadata; (3) sync-dev-root's per-candidate-SHA venv directory means a failed/partial install can never mutate the incumbent's own venv; (4) the new real subprocess signed-intake test; and that no supervisor tick-level or archive/TaskStore code was touched.
